info.name: Finalysis API
info.description: Requests for the Finalysis backend, with tests. Run top to bottom against the local dev app (`./mvnw spring-boot:run`) on a **freshly reset** dev database (`scripts/reset-dev-db.sh`): setup creates the accounts, so a second run fails. File uploads use paths relative to the repo root: run newman from there (`npx newman run postman/Finalysis.postman_collection.json -e postman/Finalysis-Local.postman_environment.json`), or set Postman's working directory (Settings → General) to the repo root. Uses only fictional sample data.

item.name: 1. Setup

request.description: A mapping written by hand. The Summit mapping below comes from the preview's suggestion instead.

exec: pm.test('not used yet, no warnings', () => { pm.expect(body.usedAt).to.eql(null); pm.expect(body.warnings).to.eql([]); });

request.description: Writes nothing. Stores `suggestedMapping.mapping` in `summitMapping` for the next request.

exec: pm.test('first rows shown', () => { pm.expect(body.headers).to.eql(['Trans. Date', 'Merchant Name', 'Amount']); pm.expect(body.rows.length).to.eql(10); });

request.description: Sends the preview's suggestion unedited, as the user would after checking it.

exec: pm.test('read by the OFX parser', () => pm.expect(body.parser).to.eql('ofx'));
pm.test('10 rows parsed and inserted', () => { pm.expect(body.parsed).to.eql(10); pm.expect(body.inserted).to.eql(10); pm.expect(body.duplicates).to.eql(0); });
pm.test('nothing earlier to continue from: unverified', () => { pm.expect(body.status).to.eql('IMPORTED'); pm.expect(body.balanceCheck).to.eql('UNVERIFIED'); });

item.name: Import checking May with a wrong LEDGERBAL (NEEDS_REVIEW)

request.description: The May checking statement with a `LEDGERBAL` $10.00 too high. Saved, but flagged for review.

exec: pm.test('continues April, but the balance is off', () => { pm.expect(body.status).to.eql('NEEDS_REVIEW'); pm.expect(body.balanceCheck).to.eql('FAILED'); });

item.name: Import Apex Visa April (CSV, with balances)

request.description: A card CSV has no balances, so the request sends the printed ones (from `statements-manifest.csv`).

exec: pm.test('read by the CSV parser', () => pm.expect(body.parser).to.eql('csv'));

item.description: Creates the four sample accounts, saves two CSV mappings (one by hand, one from the preview's suggestion) and imports four statements: one of each status. Strict: run against a freshly reset dev database.

exec: pm.test('printed date is the post date', () => pm.expect(body.postDateColumn).to.eql('Post Date'));

item.name: Replace Apex Visa mapping (unchanged locked fields) → 200

request.description: Editable after use: everything except sign, description columns and the printed-date column.
Writes nothing: the June file is still importable afterwards.

exec: pm.test('OFX summary only', () => pm.expect(body).to.eql({format: 'ofx', periodStart: '2026-06-01', periodEnd: '2026-06-30', transactionCount: 10}));
pm.test('read by the OFX parser', () => pm.expect(body.parser).to.eql('ofx'));
pm.test('money is a string with two decimals', () => pm.expect(body.closingBalance).to.eql('4066.58'));
pm.test('warnings stored with the statement', () => pm.expect(body.warnings.some(w => w.startsWith('balance unverified'))).to.be.true);
pm.test('no opening: it is set from April only when continuity passes', () => pm.expect(body.openingBalance).to.eql(null));
pm.test('newest period first', () => { for (let i = 1; i < items.length; i++) pm.expect(items[i - 1].periodStart >= items[i].periodStart).to.be.true; });

pm.test('counts and warning count, no warnings', () => { pm.expect(items[0]).to.have.property('parsedCount'); pm.expect(items[0]).to.have.property('transactionCount'); pm.expect(items[0]).to.have.property('warningCount'); pm.expect(items[0]).to.not.have.property('warnings'); });

item.name: 6. Errors

exec: pm.test('Reports name and lastFour', () => { pm.expect(fields).to.include('name'); pm.expect(fields).to.include('lastFour'); });

item.name: PUT with a column not in headers → 400

exec: pm.test('names dateColumn', () => pm.expect(error.message).to.eql('is not one of the headers'));
pm.test('sign is required for cards', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().errors).to.deep.include({field: 'sign', message: 'is required for credit card accounts'}));

item.name: PUT with a bad date format → 400
GET mapping of an account without one → 404
PUT locked field after use → 409 mapping-locked
PUT locked field, confirmed → 200 with warning

request.description: Puts the mapping back so the Apex account can keep importing its CSV files.

item.name: Imports

request.description: Any file with an extension other than .ofx, .qfx, .csv or .txt.

exec: pm.test('says why, without file contents', () => pm.expect(body.detail).to.include('DTD declarations'));

item.name: Checking file to the savings account → 422 account-mismatch
CSV import without a mapping → 422 mapping-required

exec: pm.test('headers and status, but no data rows', () => { pm.expect(body.preview.mappingStatus).to.eql('MISMATCH'); pm.expect(body.preview.headers[0]).to.eql('Trans. Date'); pm.expect(body.preview).to.not.have.property('rows'); });

item.name: Preview of a disallowed file → 415 unsupported-format

item.description: Reachable from sample files. Not covered here (the backend tests cover them): `payload-too-large` (needs a file over 10 MB), `unsupported-currency` (no non-USD sample), `ambiguous-format` and `mapping-changed` (need a test-only parser or a concurrent mapping save).
Every request here is refused, and nothing is written (except the confirmed mapping change, which is restored).
